claims.text: The tested coating is a FeNiCrCoCu high-entropy alloy on a conventional metal substrate.
Formation of a third-body layer governs the coating's wear resistance during sliding.
Microstructure refinement governs microscopic deformation during sliding.
Cu and Ti promote oxide formation and thereby accelerate formation of a protective third-body layer.
The controlled compositional intervention is the addition of both Cu and Ti.
Friction stir processing refines the microstructure through dynamic recrystallization.
Annealing after friction stir processing produces a more homogeneous, defect-free, redefined microstructure.
Friction stir processing can improve wear performance by refining grains and increasing microhardness.
The predictions apply in a high-temperature sliding regime.
The applicable sliding-velocity range is 0.5-3.5 m/s.
The applicable sliding-distance range is 500-2000 m.
Friction-induced heating causes dislocation activity that reduces residual stress and specific wear rate.
Adding Cu and Ti and applying friction stir processing followed by annealing will improve wear resistance.
The intervention will reduce microscopic deformation.
The intervention is expected to decrease the coefficient of friction.
The baseline is a conventional metal substrate without any high-entropy-alloy coating.
Load, surface roughness, and environmental conditions may alter wear resistance and microscopic deformation.
Specific wear rate and coefficient of friction can be measured in the proposed sliding tests, while SEM can characterize worn-surface morphology.
Failure to decrease both specific wear rate and coefficient of friction, together with failure to observe microstructure refinement, would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The initial alloy is already identified as FeNiCrCoCu and therefore already contains Cu, yet the intervention is described as adding Cu and Ti. Adding Ti would also change the modified alloy to a Ti-containing system that is no longer accurately denoted FeNiCrCoCu, and no base or modified composition is specified.

The baseline is an uncoated conventional substrate, whereas the intervention simultaneously introduces a coating, changes its chemistry, applies friction stir processing, and anneals it. This is inconsistent with presenting the experiment as a single controlled coating change and prevents attribution to Cu/Ti or processing.
